How this is scored

Graded directly against the seven sections of the Einstein 15-Minute Quote Call script — updated 2026-09-24. Each section is scored on its own criteria below; there's no separate rapport or process-discipline line in this version, since those behaviors (real silence held, nothing repeated) are graded inside the relevant section instead.

1. Open10 pts
5
Quid pro quo
Time-boxed ask + promise of a dependable quote, and the rep waits for a yes before continuing. Partial if rushed past, zero if skipped entirely.
3
Discovery basics
Name, moving day, city-to-city route, and approximate size — all four asked for full credit.
2
Virtual walkthrough branch
Offered correctly when the first stop is 1,800 sq ft+. Full credit if the home is under that size (nothing to offer).
2. Their Concerns30 pts
8
Their agenda
"Other than price, what are your biggest concerns... what do you want answers to on this call?" Full if asked before probing, partial if late, zero if never.
15
Two layers deep
Real follow-up on a raised concern — "tell me more" — not one question and a pivot. Heaviest single item on the whole card. Full credit if the customer never raised a concern at all.
7
Active listening reflection
"So what I'm hearing is ___, ___ and ___. Did I get all of it?" Full credit if no concerns were raised.
3. Probing for Details20 pts
12
Logistics details gathered
Property type, floor, rooms, walking distance, additional rooms, special considerations, additional stops — full credit for all/nearly all seven.
4
Packing services offered
Binary — asked or not asked.
4
Box count / overflow check
Binary — asked or not asked.
4. The Estimate10 pts
4
Anchored, personalized estimate
A typical range AND personalized to this move = full credit. Range only = partial.
3
Pricing framing
Fee transparency upfront + the "not a guess" / 2.5-hour-minimum commitment framing. Both = full, one = partial.
3
"Does that feel fair?" + silence
Asked, and followed by an actual pause — no immediate re-pitch.
5. Two Promises10 pts
4
On-Time Guarantee delivered
Covers the discount terms (starts discounting immediately if late) in recognizable form.
4
No Worries Damage Coverage delivered
$2,000 coverage, no deductible / no fine print, built into the rate (not an add-on).
2
Closes the loop
"Does that put those to rest?" asked, and nothing already covered gets repeated.
6. Concerns Again10 pts
5
Genuine final concerns check
"What's still concerning you about this move?" — not the throwaway "any questions?"
3
Follow-up on remaining concern
Real digging in if something is raised here. Full credit if nothing was raised.
2
Catch-all asked
"Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?" — binary.
7. Ask for the Business10 pts
5
Explicit ask, no easy out
"Would you like our help with your move?" asked plainly — never softened into an out like "or I can just email this over."
2
Rate-lock / no-deposit mentioned
Binary.
3
Booking confirmed with details
Date, phone, window, crew size, addresses confirmed, and notes left for the crew.

Walkthrough exception: calls cleanly routed to a virtual walkthrough before pricing (the Section 1 branch, large moves) get Sections 4–7 scored as full credit rather than zeroed — pricing was never supposed to happen on this call. Only for a clean, by-design handoff, not a call that just trails off. Sections 1–3 still score normally.

💪 Top strength
Joanna handled a complex, multi-move scenario with two storage units, appliances, and a prior negative experience with exceptional logistics clarity — she probed thoroughly, gathered detailed inventory, offered a two-truck solution to avoid the repeat-trip problem, and secured a first-move booking despite the customer's stated intent to shop competitors.

Move 'Their Agenda' to the very beginning of discovery (before any logistics questions) and ask it as written: 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move, and what do you want answers to on this call?' — it should be asked first, not after name/email/date have already been collected.

pricing_framing: "Rep discloses trip fee ($2,025), explains hourly rate ($192/hr for two movers), lists what's included (fuel, taxes, insurance, pads, wraps, tools, disassembly/reassembly). Mentions 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments. No hidden fees stated multiple times. However, there is confusion around whether the $2,025 trip fee is charged separately or included, and rep's explanation of packing material charges creates back-and-forth friction."
feels_fair_then_silence: "Never asked. Rep gives estimate and customer immediately asks clarifying questions about pricing structure. No 'Does that feel fair to you?' or similar pause for reflection."
on_time_guarantee_delivered: "Rep says 'Our on time guarantee. So, if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill and all of that is included at no extra cost.' Covers discount framing clearly."
damage_coverage_delivered: "Rep says 'we'll provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages. Unlike our competitors, so either charge extra or offer only state mandated 60¢ per pound coverage' and 'it's included in the hourly rate, no additional cost.' Covers amount, no deductible framing, and built-in status."
closes_the_loop: "Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar after delivering the Two Promises. No explicit loop-close."
final_concerns_check: "Rep asks 'Will there be anything else?' which is a throwaway yes/no. Not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent."
catch_all_asked: "No. Never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar catch-all."
explicit_ask: "Rep says 'So would you like to, would you like our help with your, with your move for Monday September 28th?' This is a plain ask. However, customer deflects with a timing question, and rep then pivots immediately into logistical details (8:30 AM start time, same-day delivery) and the customer says 'Yeah, please send the quote. I will respond to you.' The call ends without a clear yes-to-booking, so while the ask was made plainly, there was an implicit out: 'send me the quote and I'll get back to you.' This is borderline; the ask was direct but the follow-through allowed an easy escape."
rate_lock_mentioned: "Yes. Rep says 'we don't collect a front payment, no deposit as well' which signals rate is locked without deposit."
booking_confirmed: "Partial. Rep confirms: arrival window (8:30 AM–9:00 AM, trying for 8:00 AM), date (Monday September 28th), pickup address (implied from earlier), delivery address (Plano, stated). But customer never fully commits to the booking—only asks to receive the quote via email. Phone number is never confirmed, and no crew notes about customer's concerns (boxes, TV, bunk bed) are explicitly noted for the crew."

💪 Top strength
Exceptional logistics probing and detail-gathering—the rep extracted a complete, accurate picture of a complex three-unit move across multiple floors with specific big-item inventory, access constraints, and travel distance, all of which informed a credible time and price estimate.
🎯 Coaching note
Critical gap: never deliver the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) with the depth and framing required by the script, and never ask the closing 'Does that feel fair?' check before moving to booking—these are load-bearing elements that build confidence and close objections before the ask.
📅 Booking outcome
Customer explicitly agreed to reserve the truck for Saturday with a confirmed 12:30 to 1:00 PM arrival window: 'Yes, that's what I would prefer' and 'Yeah, let's do the 12:30 to one.'
Evidence quotes
quid_pro_quo: "Rep says 'I'd love to go ahead and give you that quote before. I do, I will need a couple of pieces of information' — no time-boxed framing, no 'dependable quote' promise, no wait for yes before continuing."
their_agenda: "Never asked. Rep pivots directly to logistics probing: 'Do you have any just top of mind, concerns or questions outside of the price' but then immediately moves into 'Let me take a few pieces of information' without genuine exploration of concerns."
logistics_details_gathered: "Excellent detail: property type (storage facility, apartment), floors (3rd at pickup, 2nd at delivery), room count (1 bedroom), storage unit sizes (10x10, 2x 5x10), elevator access, parking access, distance (~20 min), square footage (800), specific big items (washer/dryer, king bed, 75-inch TV), boxes (~under 20), and full addresses."
estimate_anchor: "Rep gives range ($1,236–$1,442 for 6–7 hours at $206/hr) personalized to the move (three storage units, elevator access, 20-min distance, second-floor delivery), but no initial time-boxed promise or framing before diving into logistics; estimate arrived after extensive probing."
pricing_framing: "Full: fee transparency ($206/hr includes taxes, insurance, travel, No Worries damage coverage, no start fees or credit card fees), 2.5-hour minimum disclosed, pay-for-time-used commitment stated ('you only pay for the time you use with us anyway'), and 15-minute-increments logic embedded ('if you use less than what we estimated you will only pay for the time used')."
feels_fair_then_silence: "Never asked. Rep says 'Okay, so did you want me to at least go ahead and, and reserve that truck and then once we get the pictures, we can kind of adjust accordingly' — this is a direct move to booking, not a 'does that feel fair' check with silence."
on_time_guarantee: "Not delivered. No mention of on-time discount or guarantee at all."
damage_coverage: "Mentioned in passing ('the nowhere we damage coverage is already in that') but no detail on $2,000 coverage, no-deductible framing, or 'no fine print' language."
closes_the_loop: "No. Rep does not ask if Two Promises concerns are addressed; moves directly to booking."
final_concerns_check: "Rep asks 'And then did you have any other questions' — this is the throwaway empty-question version, not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move' framing."
explicit_ask: "Never explicitly asked. Customer is never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' — rep instead says 'So did you want me to at least go ahead and reserve that truck' and customer responds affirmatively to the truck reservation, but no direct ask for the business itself."
booking_confirmed: "Partial. Confirmed: date (Saturday, start time 12:30–1:00), phone (implicit from earlier), crew size (2 movers + 1 truck), addresses (pickup and delivery). Missing: explicit confirmation of all details together, and no notes left with crew about customer concerns (customer worried it might take less than 3 hours, but no evidence this was documented for the crew)."

💪 Top strength
Chauntelle gathered exceptionally detailed logistics information across two properties (1,300 sq ft apartment with 24 fake plants, 70-inch TV, piano excluded, plus mother's 500 sq ft independent living room with 70-inch TV), asked follow-up questions to clarify furniture specifics (sectional vs. sofa, TV sizes, soil in planters), and confirmed walking distances and floor accessibility—this level of detail directly supported her estimate accuracy.
🎯 Coaching note
Chauntelle skipped the high-value Section 1 'quid pro quo' framing (the 10–15 minute time-box + promise of dependable quote + waiting for a yes), which is the single load-bearing line on the call card; without it, the customer never consented to the call structure, and the call felt like a facts-gathering session rather than a guided sales conversation—reintroduce this framing at the top of every intake call before any probing begins.

quid_pro_quo: "Rep never delivered recognizable framing about 10–15 minute call or promise of dependable quote before launching into discovery. Jumped directly into 'I'll walk through this and then you can tell me what changes need to be made.'"

two_layers_deep: "Customer raised concern about licensing/insurance and bad prior experience with low-budget movers. Rep followed up: 'We are... Customer then elaborated further on her concerns about mover training/professionalism, and rep engaged on that topic."
active_listening_reflection: "No summary reflection. Rep acknowledged the concern ('Oh I'm so sorry about that') and pivoted directly to Einstein's credentials rather than reflecting back what was heard."
estimate_anchor: "Rep gave hourly rate ($200/hr for 2 movers, 26-foot truck) and estimated 8–9 hours for a total of $1,775–$1,975, personalized by mentioning the customer's prep level and specific items. Included note about customer paying only for time used."
pricing_framing: "Rep disclosed trip fee ($105, already included), no hidden fees, no credit card fees, and mentioned travel/taxes/insurance included. Did mention 'no worries damage coverage' covers up to $2,000 but did not explicitly frame the 2.5-hour minimum or 15-minute-increment commitment."
feels_fair_then_silence: "Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent. Instead transitioned immediately into explaining the estimate flexibility and time-based billing."
on_time_guarantee_delivered: "Rep mentioned 'on time guarantee' by name but did not cover the discount terms—did not explain that Einstein discounts immediately if late, only that 'we have a truck available first thing in the morning with the start time between 8:00 and 10.'"
damage_coverage_delivered: "Full coverage delivered: 'no worries damage coverage. That is also on top of like our insurance which covers up to $2,000 for any kind of incidentals' and framed as built-in ('that's also on top of like our insurance')."
closes_the_loop: "Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar. Instead moved directly into booking and truck availability."
final_concerns_check: "Asked as 'Are there any other questions that I can answer?' — the generic throwaway version with no genuine emotional specificity."
catch_all_asked: "Never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all."
explicit_ask: "Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent. Instead offered to send quote and said 'you can honestly just reply and say, okay, hey, yes, let's go ahead and book it or you could give us a call' — soft-landed without explicit ask. rate_lock_mentioned: "Rep mentioned 'There is no deposit if you need to cancel if you need to change it if you need to modify it we don't have fees for that either' — this protects the customer's rate but does not explicitly promise the rate is locked."
booking_confirmed: "Partial. Rep did not attempt to book at all — customer declined ('I'm still getting quotes I gotta get at least two of them'). No date/phone/arrival window/crew size/addresses confirmed for a reservation. Rep only confirmed sending an email quote."

💪 Top strength
Calvin handled a high-pressure, last-minute logistics problem with poise: the customer needed help on an impossible timeline with a heavy safe and furniture, and Calvin offered transparent pricing, equipment solutions (dolly types, 3-man crew upgrade), and clear next steps without panic or false promises.
🎯 Coaching note
Start every call with the scripted quid pro quo (time-boxed ask + promise of dependable quote) and wait for a yes before probing; also ask their agenda upfront ('Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?') to surface and validate what matters most to them, rather than jumping into problem-solving mode on the first issue they mention.
